clauses.title: 1. Who we are
clauses.text:
This Privacy Policy explains how {{business.name}} ("we", "us") handles personal data when you use {{product.name}} (the "Service"). It applies to visitors, account holders and people who write to us.

We decide why and how your personal data is used for the Service, so we are the "controller" (in Korea, the "personal information handler"). Our address is {{business.address}}. Our business registration number is {{business.regNo}}.

Our privacy officer (the person responsible for personal data) is {{business.owner}}, Representative. Write to {{business.email}} or use our Contact page (/contact).

This policy takes effect on {{legal.effectiveDate}}.

clauses.title: 2. What we collect, why, and for how long
clauses.text:
We collect only what the Service needs. Here is each kind of data, why we use it, and how long we keep it.

- Account data: your name, email address, password (stored only as a one-way hash), language and time zone. Why: to create your account and let you sign in. Kept: until you delete your account, plus a {{product.deletionGraceDays}}-day grace period.
- Sign-in with Google, Kakao or Naver: the name, email address and account ID that the provider shares with us. Kakao may not share an email address. Why: to sign you in. Kept: as account data.
- Age and agreement records: your confirmation that you are 14 or older, which version of the Terms and Privacy Policy you accepted, and when. Why: to prove the agreement. Kept: as account data.
- Devices and sessions: when and from which device you signed in (IP address and browser type). Why: security, and so you can sign out other devices. Kept: while the session or account exists.
- Plan and billing status: your plan, its status and dates, and a reference to your payment at Paddle. We do not receive your full card number. Why: to give you the plan you paid for. Kept: while the account exists; some records for longer as the law requires (see section 7).
- Messages you send us: your name (optional), contact details, message and request number. Why: to answer you. Kept: {{product.inquiryRetentionDays}} days after we finish, or 3 years if the message is a complaint or dispute about a purchase.
- Marketing choices: whether you agreed to marketing emails, and when. Why: to send only what you agreed to and to prove it. Kept: while the account exists, and for 3 years after you delete your account, as proof of what you agreed to if there is a dispute. This kept record has no name or email address.
- Usage analytics (only if you accept analytics): pages viewed, clicks, and how you reached the site, with a random ID. Why: to improve the Service. Kept: until you withdraw consent or delete your account.
- Security and error data: IP address, browser details, rate-limit counters and error reports, with personal details masked where possible. Why: to keep the Service safe and fix faults. Kept: for a short time, and administrators' access logs for 1 year.
- Bot check: when a form uses a bot check, Cloudflare Turnstile reads your IP address, browser details and a device fingerprint. Why: to stop automated abuse.

We do not use your data for advertising. We do not sell your data. We do not use it for automated decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects on you.

clauses.title: 3. Why we are allowed to use your data
clauses.text:
Where the law asks for a legal basis (for example in the EU and UK), we rely on these.

- Contract: to create your account, give you the Service and handle your plan.
- Consent: for analytics and for marketing emails. You can withdraw it at any time.
- Legal obligation: to keep tax, payment and consumer records, and to answer your rights requests.
- Legitimate interests: to keep the Service secure, prevent abuse and fix faults, in a way that respects your rights.

In Korea, we process personal information under the Personal Information Protection Act: with your consent, to carry out our contract with you, to follow the law, or as that Act otherwise allows.

clauses.title: 4. Cookies and similar technologies
clauses.text:
We use these cookies and storage items.

- Strictly necessary: the sign-in session cookie, security and bot-check items, and your cookie choice. The Service cannot work without them, so they do not need your consent.
- Analytics (only with your consent): PostHog may set a cookie or local storage item with a random ID. Until you accept, it is switched off and records nothing.

We ask for analytics consent in the banner at the bottom of the page. You can choose "Reject all" and still use everything. To change your choice later, clear this site's cookies and storage in your browser settings, and the banner asks you again, or write to us on our Contact page (/contact). You can also block cookies in your browser settings, but then sign-in may not work.

clauses.title: 5. Who receives your data
clauses.text:
We share data only with companies that help us run the Service, and only what they need. We do not sell personal data, and we do not share it for advertising across other companies' sites.

- Paddle (payments, Merchant of Record): your name, email, country, tax details and payment details. Paddle is an independent controller of this data. Its privacy notice applies: https://www.paddle.com/legal/privacy
- Vercel (website hosting): requests to the site, including IP address and logs.
- Supabase (database hosting): the data we store for your account. Stored in {{legal.databaseRegion}}.
- Resend (email sending): your email address and the content of the emails we send.
- PostHog (analytics, only with your consent): the usage events described above.
- Sentry (error reports): error details with personal data masked.
- Cloudflare Turnstile (bot check): the data described in section 2.
- Google, Kakao and Naver (if you sign in with them): they know that you signed in to us. Their privacy notices apply to what they hold.

We also disclose data if the law or a court requires it, or to protect rights and safety. Our providers may use the data only to give their service to us. Paddle and the sign-in providers are the exception: they act for themselves.

clauses.title: 6. Transfers to other countries
clauses.text:
We and our providers are in different countries, so your data can be processed outside the country where you live, including in the United States. For people in Korea, we transfer data abroad because it is needed to carry out our contract with you, and we tell you about it here, as the Personal Information Protection Act allows. For people in the EU, EEA or UK, we rely on the safeguards or other grounds that the GDPR allows, such as standard contractual clauses, your consent, or the need to carry out our contract with you.

For people in Korea, the table at the end of this page lists the companies that receive data abroad, the country, what they receive and why, how long they keep it, and how to refuse. It includes Supabase (our database, stored in {{legal.databaseRegion}}) and Sentry (error reports). Supabase is a company outside Korea, so we list it even where the data is stored in the region shown. You can refuse a transfer, but then we may not be able to give you the Service.

clauses.title: 7. How long we keep data, and what the law makes us keep
clauses.text:
We keep data only as long as we need it for the reasons in section 2. Then we delete it or make it anonymous.

Some records must be kept longer by law. We keep them apart from your account, with no name or email, only a masked reference. They are deleted when the period ends.

- Records about advertising and labelling: 6 months.
- Records about contracts and withdrawal from contracts: 5 years.
- Records about payment and supply of goods or services: 5 years.
- Records about complaints and disputes: 3 years.
- Access logs of staff who open personal data: 1 year.

Source: Korean Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, Article 6 and its Enforcement Decree, Article 6; Korean Personal Information Protection Act, Article 21; Korean Standard on Safety Measures for Personal Information, Article 8 (access logs).

Paddle keeps its own records of your payments as an independent controller, for the period its privacy notice states.

clauses.title: 8. Deleting your account and your data
9. Your rights and how to use them
10. Marketing emails
clauses.text:
We send marketing emails only if you agreed. The box at sign-up is never ticked for you.

Every marketing email shows who sent it, how to contact us, and an unsubscribe link that works without signing in. In Korea the subject starts with "(광고)" (Korean for "advertisement") and the unsubscribe notice is in Korean and English.

After you agree or withdraw, we send you a written confirmation within 14 days that shows who we are, what you chose, the date, and the result. Every 2 years we ask you to confirm that you still want these emails. If you do not confirm, we stop.

Service messages, such as security and plan notices, are not marketing and are not affected by this choice.

clauses.title: 11. Children
clauses.text: The Service is for people aged 14 and over. We ask you to confirm your age when you sign up. We do not knowingly collect data from children under 14. If you think a child under 14 has given us data, tell us on our Contact page (/contact) and we will delete it.

clauses.title: 12. Security
clauses.text: We protect your data with measures such as encryption in transit, hashed passwords, access control, rate limits, bot checks and logs of staff access. No system is perfectly safe. If a breach is likely to harm you, we tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

clauses.title: 13. Rules for your region
clauses.text:
Korea. We follow the Personal Information Protection Act. Our privacy contact is named in section 1. The table at the end of this page covers transfers abroad.

EU, EEA and UK. The legal bases are in section 3. You have the rights in section 9 under the GDPR and the UK GDPR, including the right to complain to your supervisory authority. Our providers' transfer safeguards are described in section 6.

California, USA. In the last 12 months we collected the kinds of data listed in section 2 for the purposes given there, and shared them with the providers in section 5. We do not sell personal information and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. You can ask to know, delete, correct, or limit use of sensitive data, and you will not be treated worse for asking. Use the ways in section 9. We answer within 45 days.

clauses.title: 14. Changes to this policy
clauses.text: We may update this policy. For changes that matter, we email you at least 30 days before they apply, and we show the new effective date at the top of this page. We record which version you accepted when you signed up. Earlier versions are available if you ask us.
